chunks: From him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Hamdan al-Qalanisi, from Ishaq ibn Bunnan, from Ibn Baqqah, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A woman claimed against her husband during the time of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) that he did not have intercourse with her, and he claimed that he did. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ordered her to apply saffron, then he would wash his penis. If the water came out yellow, he was believed; otherwise, he was ordered to divorce her. The way to reconcile these narrations is that the Imam has discretion in this matter, to rule as he wishes, based on what appears to him in the moment of certainty or taking precaution in acting upon one of these matters.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali resolve a dispute over sexual consummation between a husband and wife?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s al-Istibsar outlines a specific judicial mechanism (istifrar) used by Imam Ali (AS) to resolve marital disputes over consummation, utilizing saffron as a visual indicator for semen. It highlights the Imam’s pragmatic approach, balancing definitive proof with precautionary measures, which later Shia jurists cite to justify judicial discretion in verifying sexual claims. The procedure underscores the importance of empirical evidence in early Islamic family law while maintaining flexibility based on the Imam’s assessment of the situation.
